shots.text: Before the Concord, before the Spire, before anyone kept count of the years... there were seven kingdoms.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: An old painted map coming out of darkness: six kingdoms in a ring, each under its own crown and colour (red, blue-white, green, teal, ochre, violet), and a seventh, colourless, in the middle.

shots.text:
Six were bound to the elements of their lands. The seventh ruled the middle of the world.

And he wanted all of it.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Six crowned monarchs, each lit by their element: a forge-king, a horse-king, a green queen, a sea-queen, a mountain-king, a star-queen. Then the middle kingdom's black-walled capital, and on its throne a king in black with a tall crown of six empty sockets.

shots.text: His name was Vael-Orrun, the High King. Where his armies marched, fire would not burn, and the wind lay down and died.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The High King's armies crossing a burning land; behind them the flames freeze into grey glass, the grass stops moving, a river hangs still in mid-fall.

shots.text:
The six hated one another. They stood together anyway, each beside its oldest enemy, and drove him out past the edge of the stars.

We call it the Ring.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The six monarchs in a ring around the burning black city, hands joined, Fire across from Water, Storm across from Earth, Nature across from Void. The High King is flung out through the edge of a starfield into darkness.

shots.text:
They could not kill him. So they locked the door with his own crown, and gave their lives to hold it. On the ruins of his city, we built Solenne.

My city.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The crown shattering into a six-coloured crystal, the Heartstone. The six monarchs fading into a volcano, a storm, a tree, a sea, a mountain, a starless sky. Then dawn over Solenne: six white walls rising on black ruins, the Heartstone glowing at the centre, the golden Sunstone above.

shots.text: Six years ago, a man I loved like a father lost his daughter to the dark. The exiled king made him a promise.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Night. Cassivane Dral, the Lord Marshal, alone on a balcony, holding a gold locket. Over his shoulder, in the stars, the faint crown-shaped gap. His face is in shadow.

shots.text: On the night of the Black Comet, the edge of the world split open.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The Hollow Rift: violet grass, a ring of black pillars singing with stolen light. A black comet crosses the sky. The ground at the centre tears open into a crack full of nothing.

shots.text: Oswin, the Grey Lantern, held it for one night. At dawn, he walked to the edge... and gave it every light he had.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Oswin, old, grey robes and hat, walks to the lip of the Crack with his lantern-staff raised. Behind him a line of Spirewright towers burning in six colours. Grey shapes crawling out of the Crack.

shots.text:
The Crack closed to a hairline.

And Oswin fell. His lantern went out.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: A blast of white light; the Crack slams almost shut. The ground under Oswin gives way. He falls into the dark, the lantern going out. Last frame: one tiny spark still drifting down after him.

shots.text:
But a voice can pass through a hairline. It drove the six sleeping monarchs mad, and set each land against the one across from it.

The High King has come back for what was his.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Six quick cuts: a volcano burning grey, a stormcloud gone solid black, a giant tree rotting, a frozen sea heaving, a mountain opening grey eyes, a starless sky with a crown. Then hordes of grey-eyed elemental spirits pouring across the land toward each other.

shots.text:
We cannot win back the lands. We can only hold the roads until their people escape.

Every road we hold will cost us a city.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: A long line of refugees with carts on an ash road. Tamsin Reed with her lantern-pole waving them on. A gloved hand sets a glowing keystone into the foundation of a stone tower.

shots.text:
I am Ysolde, Queen of a city that is running out of cities. And you, Spirewright, are the last of Oswin's apprentices.

Hold the road.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Queen Ysolde on the white walls of Solenne, looking east toward smoke on the horizon. Title card.
